2. But the rank theorem is much cleaner

Here is the really beautiful part.

Take a block-constant observable

\[
f=\sum_{j=1}^k c_j1_{B_j}.
\]

For \(x\in B_i\),

\[
(Kf)(x)=f(Tx)=c_{q}
\]

where \(q\) is the target block containing \(T(x)\).

For \(Kf\) to remain block-constant on \(B_i\), all target blocks reached by \(B_i\) must have the same coefficient.

Define

\[
S_i=\{j:M_{ij}>0\}.
\]

Then

\[
Df=0
\]

iff

\[
c_j=c_\ell
\qquad
\text{whenever }j,\ell\in S_i
\]

for every \(i\).

Now make a graph whose vertices are the partition blocks and connect \(j\) and \(\ell\) whenever they occur together in some \(S_i\).

Call it \(H_M\).

Then:

\[
Df=0
\]

iff \(f\)'s coefficient vector is constant on every connected component of \(H_M\).

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\dim\ker D=c(H_M)
}
\]

and hence

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{rank}D=k-c(H_M).
}
\]

This is the theorem I want to attack.

Not because it sounds impressive.

Because it explains something.


---

3. The conceptual split is excellent

Structural layer

\operatorname{supp}(M)
\longrightarrow
H_M
\longrightarrow

\longrightarrow
\operatorname{rank}D.
\]

Metric layer

Actual multiplicities matter:

\[
M
\longrightarrow
D^TD
\longrightarrow
\sigma(D)
\longrightarrow
\|D\|_F,\|D\|_2.
\]

So we potentially have:

\[
\boxed{\text{support determines rank}}
\]

while

\[
\boxed{\text{weights determine geometry}.}
\]

That is a much better story than simply “AQARION has a defect operator.”

This one is particularly important.

=

Numerically, that's one test.

Exactly, over rationals, that's another.

Dimension equality alone can hide implementation errors.

Equality of the actual subspaces is much stronger.

## 2. Correct theorem: support determines the restricted kernel

Let

$$
\Pi=\{B_1,\dots,B_k\},\qquad b_i=|B_i|,
$$

and let $$V_\Pi\subseteq\mathbb R^X$$ be the block-constant subspace. Define

$$
D=(I-P_\Pi)K_TP_\Pi,
\qquad
(K_Tf)(x)=f(Tx).
$$

For each source block, let

$$
S_i=\{j:M_{ij}>0\},
\qquad
M_{ij}=|\{x\in B_i:T(x)\in B_j\}|.
$$

Define $$H_M$$ on all $$k$$ target-block labels, including isolated vertices. Connect distinct $$j,\ell$$ when they belong to the same $$S_i$$.

For

$$
f=\sum_j c_j1_{B_j},
$$

the value $$K_Tf(x)$$ is $$c_j$$ when $$T(x)\in B_j$$. Consequently,

$$
Df=0
\iff
c_j=c_\ell
\quad\text{whenever }j,\ell\in S_i.
$$

Taking transitive closure gives:

$$
\boxed{
\ker(D|_{V_\Pi})
=
\left\{
\sum_jc_j1_{B_j}:
c\text{ is constant on each component of }H_M
\right\}.
}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dim\ker(D|_{V_\Pi})=c(H_M),
$$

and

$$
\boxed{\operatorname{rank}D=k-c(H_M).}
$$

### Ambient-kernel correction

The synthesis wrote $$\dim\ker D=c(H_M)$$. That is false when $$D$$ denotes the full $$n\times n$$ operator.

Because $$D=DP_\Pi$$, it annihilates $$V_\Pi^\perp$$. The actual ambient kernel is

$$
\boxed{
\ker D
=
V_\Pi^\perp
\oplus
\ker(D|_{V_\Pi}).
}
$$

Hence

$$
\boxed{
\dim\ker D=n-k+c(H_M).
}
$$

The rank theorem survives unchanged. The kernel theorem needs this domain correction.

## 3. Exact local energy decomposition

For an observable $$f=\sum_jc_j1_{B_j}$$, define

$$
p_{ij}=\frac{M_{ij}}{b_i}.
$$

The average of $$K_Tf$$ over source block $$B_i$$ is

$$
\bar c_i=\sum_jp_{ij}c_j.
$$

Thus

$$
\boxed{
\|Df\|^2
=
\sum_i b_i
\left(
\sum_jp_{ij}c_j^2
-
\left(\sum_jp_{ij}c_j\right)^2
\right).
}
$$

Each source block contributes a weighted variance. Equivalently,

$$
\boxed{
\|Df\|^2
=
\sum_i\frac1{b_i}
\sum_{j<\ell}
M_{ij}M_{i\ell}(c_j-c_\ell)^2.
}
$$

This expression simultaneously explains:

- Why support controls the kernel.
- Why multiplicity controls the strength of each disagreement.
- Why a source block contributes zero exactly when its observable target values agree.

### Frobenius correction

Taking the trace in the normalized block basis gives

$$
\|D\|_F^2
=
\sum_{i,j}\frac{M_{ij}}{b_j}
-
\sum_{i,j}\frac{M_{ij}^2}{b_ib_j}.
$$

But this is identically

$$
\boxed{
\|D\|_F^2
=
\sum_{i,j}
\frac{M_{ij}(b_i-M_{ij})}{b_ib_j}.
}
$$

No additional hypothesis is required:

$$
\frac{M_{ij}(b_i-M_{ij})}{b_ib_j}
=
\frac{M_{ij}}{b_j}
-
\frac{M_{ij}^2}{b_ib_j}.
$$

The later synthesis incorrectly rejected this compact formula. Retain it.

The distinct earlier expression with first term $$M_{ij}/(b_ib_j)$$, however, is generally wrong.

## 5. D7 completed: identical support, different spectrum

Use the same partition in both systems:

$$
B_1=\{0,1,2,3\},
\qquad
B_2=\{4,5,6,7\}.
$$

Choose

$$
T_1=,[0][4]
$$

$$
T_2=.[4][0]
$$

Their multiplicity matrices are

$$
M_1=
\begin{pmatrix}
3&1\\
4&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M_2=
\begin{pmatrix}
2&2\\
4&0
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

They have exactly the same entrywise support:

$$
\operatorname{supp}M_1=\operatorname{supp}M_2.
$$

Both support graphs consist of one edge joining the two block labels, so both have defect rank one.

The exact matrix computation returned:

| Quantity | System 1 | System 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| $$\operatorname{rank}D$$ | 1 | 1 |
| $$\|D\|_F^2$$ | $$3/8$$ | $$1/2$$ |
| Nonzero eigenvalue of $$D^\top D$$ | $$3/8$$ | $$1/2$$ |
| Nonzero singular value | $$\sqrt{3/8}$$ | $$1/\sqrt2$$ |
| Characteristic polynomial of $$D^\top D$$ | $$\lambda^7(\lambda-3/8)$$ | $$\lambda^7(\lambda-1/2)$$ |

This is the requested separation:

$$
\boxed{
\text{same support}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\text{same rank in this theorem},
}
$$

but

$$
\boxed{
\text{same support}
\;\not\Longrightarrow\;
\text{same energy or spectrum}.
}
$$

It is an exact counterexample to support-only spectral determination. It is not a novelty claim.

## 6. Rank-one classification follows directly

Since

$$
k-c(H_M)=\sum_{C\in\pi_0(H_M)}(|C|-1),
$$

rank one means precisely:

$$
\boxed{
H_M\text{ has one component of size two, with every other vertex isolated}.
}
$$

Rank two has two possible component-size patterns:

- One component of size three, all others isolated.
- Two components of size two, all others isolated.

The graph may have different edge configurations within a three-vertex component; component size, not triangle-versus-path structure, controls rank.

## 7. Literature positioning

The March paper by Gustav Conradie, Nicolas Boullé, Jean-Christophe Loiseau, Steven L. Brunton, and Matthew J. Colbrook explicitly studies Koopman invariance through principal angles, projection errors, diagnostics, and refinement.[1]

The May paper by Dhruv Shah and Jorge Cortés develops principal-vector subspace pruning, invariance-error refinement, and numerical update methods.[2]

Accordingly, AQARION should not claim principal-angle invariance diagnostics as new. Its defensible research focus here is:

> For partition-generated observables of finite deterministic maps, invariance failure admits an exact support-based kernel description and a multiplicity-weighted variance decomposition.

For permutation dynamics, the principal-angle specialization is appropriate because $$K_T$$ is orthogonal. For arbitrary noninjective maps, it is not an isometry under the counting inner product, so the unqualified identity $$\sigma_j(D)=\sin\theta_j$$ must not be carried over.

## 8. Two further scope guards

### Do not enumerate all maps and partitions through $$n=9$$

That proposal is not a small verification task. At $$n=9$$, the domain contains

$$
9^9B_9=9^9\cdot21{,}147
$$

instances—trillions of map–partition pairs. The paper proof and targeted exact examples are more useful now than that census.

### Repeated application of $$D$$ is not the filtration

For any idempotent $$P$$,

$$
D^2=(I-P)KP(I-P)KP=0.
$$

Therefore repeated powers of $$D$$ cannot measure persistent leakage.

The meaningful multi-step object is instead

$$
V_t=V_\Pi+K_TV_\Pi+\cdots+K_T^tV_\Pi,
$$

with

$$
g_t=\dim V_t-\dim V_\Pi.
$$

In particular,

$$
g_1=\operatorname{rank}D.
$$

Do not automatically identify this linear-span closure with a partition closure: a linear subspace generated by observables need not itself be a partition-generated observable algebra.

## Finite Pullback Rigidity and Join Closure

For a finite set \(X\), a map \(T:X\to X\), and an equivalence relation \(E\), define

\[
T^{-1}(E)=\{(x,y):T(x)\mathrel E T(y)\}.
\]

AQARION's finite pullback-rigidity lemma states

\[
T^{-1}(E)\subseteq E
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T^{-1}(E)=E.
\]

The proof uses finiteness of the quotient set \(X/E\): distinct source equivalence classes have disjoint nonempty sets of target classes, forcing each source class to map into exactly one target class. The induced map on the quotient is a permutation.

Consequently, if \(E\) and \(F\) satisfy the pullback-inclusion hypothesis, both are congruences of \(T\), and their join is also a congruence:

\[
\boxed{T^{-1}(E\vee F)=E\vee F.}
\]

The unrestricted infinite analogue under the same pullback-inclusion hypotheses is false. A separate chain argument proves join closure for relations that are already forward-preserved congruences, but does not establish the finite rigidity lemma on infinite sets.

### LRTS add-on

## LRTS — JOIN-STABILITY Research Update

**Date:** 8 October 2026

### Mathematical disposition

The finite JOIN-STABILITY theorem has a direct proof from finite pullback rigidity and closure of congruences under generated joins.

For finite \(T:X\to X\),

\[
T^{-1}(E)\subseteq E
\Longrightarrow T^{-1}(E)=E.
\]

Therefore, for two relations satisfying the hypothesis,

\[
T^{-1}(E\vee F)=E\vee F.
\]

The equality is stronger than the original inclusion claim.

### Adversarial boundary

The unrestricted infinite extension is false. The finite-cardinality argument cannot be transferred to infinite quotient sets without additional hypotheses.

The join-chain argument alone proves closure for forward-preserved congruences; it does not derive forward preservation from pullback inclusion on arbitrary infinite sets.

### `reproduce.sh` — reproduction entrypoint

Replace the current script. It now runs structural validation, the independent audit, and negative controls as separate steps. It captures output and exit codes instead of treating a missing step as success.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

mkdir -p receipts

STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
LOG="receipts/reproduction-${STAMP}.log"
STATUS="receipts/reproduction-${STAMP}.status"

set +e
{
    echo "JOIN-STABILITY reproduction"
    echo "UTC_START=${STAMP}"
    echo "PACKAGE_DIR=${ROOT}"
    echo

    echo "=== Source revision ==="
    git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" rev-parse HEAD
    REVISION_RC=$?
    echo "GIT_REVISION_EXIT=${REVISION_RC}"
    if [ "$REVISION_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 10
    fi

    echo
    echo "=== Structural verifier ==="
    python3 verify.py
    VERIFY_RC=$?
    echo "VERIFY_EXIT=${VERIFY_RC}"
    if [ "$VERIFY_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 11
    fi

    echo
    echo "=== Independent finite audit ==="
    python3 join_stability_independent_audit.py
    AUDIT_RC=$?
    echo "AUDIT_EXIT=${AUDIT_RC}"
    if [ "$AUDIT_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 12
    fi

    echo
    echo "=== Negative controls ==="
    python3 verify.py --self-test-negative-controls
    NEGATIVE_RC=$?
    echo "NEGATIVE_CONTROLS_EXIT=${NEGATIVE_RC}"
    if [ "$NEGATIVE_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 13
    fi

    echo
    echo "=== Lean status ==="
    echo "Lean compilation is not part of this script."
    echo "Lean status remains OPEN unless a separately recorded Lean build passes."

    echo
    echo "RESULT=PACKAGE_AND_AUDIT_PASS"
    echo "RESULT_SCOPE=STRUCTURAL_AND_FINITE_COMPUTATIONAL_CHECKS_ONLY"
    exit 0
} > >(tee "$LOG") 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

{
    echo "exit_code=${RC}"
    echo "log=${LOG}"
    echo "utc_start=${STAMP}"
    echo "result=$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo PACKAGE_AND_AUDIT_PASS || echo FAIL)"
} > "$STATUS"

echo "REPRODUCTION_EXIT=${RC}"
echo "REPRODUCTION_LOG=${LOG}"
echo "REPRODUCTION_STATUS=${STATUS}"

exit "$RC"
```

Operational note: this script expects to run inside a Git checkout. A ZIP-only clone without `.git` will fail closed at the revision check; that is intentional until the clone procedure supplies a separately pinned source revision.

### `verify.py` — strict package verifier

Replace the current verifier with this version. It validates required files and directories, schema and record types, registry references, revision identity, and negative controls. It does not claim to prove the theorem.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail-closed structural verifier for JOIN-STABILITY.

This program checks package integrity and declared evidence structure.
It does not prove the mathematical theorem.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SHA_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
EVIDENCE_CLASSES = {"[D]", "[P]", "[V]", "[PV]", "[C]", "[R]", "[CE]"}
CLAIM_STATUSES = {
    "DEFINITION",
    "PROVED_MATHEMATICALLY",
    "PROVED_MATHEMATICALLY_LEAN_OPEN",
    "PROVED_MATHEMATICALLY_LEAN_OPEN_REPLAY_NOT_ESTABLISHED",
    "IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE_ONLY",
    "COMPUTATIONAL_TARGET_NOT_YET_REPRODUCED",
    "REFUTED",
    "OPEN",
    "QUARANTINED",
}
REQUIRED_FILES = (
    "README.md",
    "manifest.json",
    "zip-clone.md",
    "claims.jsonl",
    "evidence.jsonl",
    "reproduce.sh",
    "verify.py",
    "join_stability_independent_audit.py",
    "AQ_DYN_PULL_RIGID-001.lean",
    "docs/finite-pullback-rigidity.md",
    "fixtures/README.md",
    "negative-controls/README.md",
    "receipts/README.md",
    "docs/README.md",
)
REQUIRED_DIRS = ("fixtures", "negative-controls", "receipts", "docs")

class VerificationError(Exception):
    pass

def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise VerificationError(message)

def read_json(path: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as exc:
        raise VerificationError(f"{path.name}: invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
    require(isinstance(data, dict), f"{path.name}: root must be an object")
    return data

def read_jsonl(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    records = []
    try:
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise VerificationError(f"{path.name}: cannot read: {exc}") from exc

    for line_no, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        try:
            record = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise VerificationError(
                f"{path.name}:{line_no}: invalid JSON: {exc}"
            ) from exc
        require(
            isinstance(record, dict),
            f"{path.name}:{line_no}: record must be an object",
        )
        records.append(record)
    return records

def unique_records(records: list[dict], key: str, source: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
    result = {}
    for index, record in enumerate(records, 1):
        value = record.get(key)
        require(
            isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip()),
            f"{source}:{index}: missing or invalid {key}",
        )
        require(value not in result, f"{source}: duplicate {key} {value!r}")
        result[value] = record
    return result

def check_manifest(manifest: dict) -> None:
    required = {
        "schema_version",
        "package_id",
        "package_version",
        "status",
        "source_revision",
        "claim_registry",
        "evidence_registry",
        "required_artifacts",
        "required_directories",
        "verification_policy",
        "audit",
        "promotion",
    }
    require(required <= manifest.keys(), "manifest: missing required fields")
    require(manifest["schema_version"] == "1.0", "manifest: unsupported schema_version")
    require(manifest["package_id"] == "JOIN-STABILITY", "manifest: wrong package_id")
    require(isinstance(manifest["package_version"], str), "manifest: package_version must be string")
    require(
        isinstance(manifest["source_revision"], str)
        and SHA_RE.fullmatch(manifest["source_revision"]),
        "manifest: source_revision must be a full 40-character lowercase commit SHA",
    )
    require(manifest["claim_registry"] == "claims.jsonl", "manifest: claim_registry must be claims.jsonl")
    require(manifest["evidence_registry"] == "evidence.jsonl", "manifest: evidence_registry must be evidence.jsonl")
    require(
        isinstance(manifest["required_artifacts"], list)
        and all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in manifest["required_artifacts"]),
        "manifest: required_artifacts must be a string array",
    )
    require(
        len(manifest["required_artifacts"]) == len(set(manifest["required_artifacts"])),
        "manifest: duplicate required artifact",
    )
    require(
        isinstance(manifest["required_directories"], list)
        and all(isinstance(x, str) and x for x in manifest["required_directories"]),
        "manifest: required_directories must be a string array",
    )
    require(
        isinstance(manifest["verification_policy"], dict),
        "manifest: verification_policy must be an object",
    )
    require(
        manifest["verification_policy"].get("fail_closed") is True,
        "manifest: fail_closed must be true",
    )
    require(
        manifest["verification_policy"].get("allow_automatic_manifest_generation") is False,
        "manifest: automatic manifest generation must be disabled",
    )
    require(isinstance(manifest["audit"], dict), "manifest: audit must be an object")
    require(isinstance(manifest["audit"].get("expected"), dict), "manifest: audit.expected must be an object")
    require(isinstance(manifest["promotion"], dict), "manifest: promotion must be an object")
    require(
        all(manifest["promotion"].get(key) is False for key in (
            "reproduction_verified", "proof_reviewed", "lean_verified", "publication_approved"
        )),
        "manifest: promotion flags must remain false in this package state",
    )

def check_claims(claims: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:
    by_id = unique_records(claims, "claim_id", "claims.jsonl")
    required = {
        "claim_id", "version", "statement", "mathematical_status",
        "evidence_class", "domain", "dependencies", "proof_artifact",
    }
    for claim_id, record in by_id.items():
        require(required <= record.keys(), f"{claim_id}: missing required claim fields")
        require(isinstance(record["version"], str), f"{claim_id}: version must be string")
        require(isinstance(record["statement"], str) and record["statement"].strip(),
                f"{claim_id}: statement must be nonempty")
        require(record["mathematical_status"] in CLAIM_STATUSES,
                f"{claim_id}: unsupported mathematical_status")
        require(record["evidence_class"] in EVIDENCE_CLASSES,
                f"{claim_id}: unsupported evidence_class")
        require(isinstance(record["domain"], str), f"{claim_id}: domain must be string")
        require(isinstance(record["dependencies"], list)
                and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in record["dependencies"]),
                f"{claim_id}: dependencies must be a string array")
        require(record["proof_artifact"] is None or isinstance(record["proof_artifact"], str),
                f"{claim_id}: proof_artifact must be string or null")
    for claim_id, record in by_id.items():
        for dependency in record["dependencies"]:
            require(dependency in by_id,
                    f"{claim_id}: unresolved dependency {dependency!r}")
    return by_id

def check_evidence(
    evidence: list[dict],
    claims: dict[str, dict],
    required_artifacts: set[str],
) -> dict[str, dict]:
    by_id = unique_records(evidence, "evidence_id", "evidence.jsonl")
    required = {
        "evidence_id", "claim_id", "class", "type",
        "artifact", "status", "description",
    }
    for evidence_id, record in by_id.items():
        require(required <= record.keys(), f"{evidence_id}: missing required evidence fields")
        require(record["claim_id"] in claims,
                f"{evidence_id}: unresolved claim_id {record['claim_id']!r}")
        require(record["class"] in EVIDENCE_CLASSES,
                f"{evidence_id}: unsupported evidence class")
        require(isinstance(record["type"], str) and record["type"],
                f"{evidence_id}: type must be nonempty string")
        require(isinstance(record["artifact"], str) and record["artifact"],
                f"{evidence_id}: artifact must be nonempty string")
        require(isinstance(record["status"], str) and record["status"],
                f"{evidence_id}: status must be nonempty string")
        require(isinstance(record["description"], str) and record["description"],
                f"{evidence_id}: description must be nonempty string")
        # Artifacts may refer to files not included in the minimal manifest,
        # but an artifact path that looks like a package-relative path must exist.
        if "/" in record["artifact"] or record["artifact"].endswith(".py"):
            require(
                (ROOT / record["artifact"]).is_file(),
                f"{evidence_id}: artifact file missing: {record['artifact']}",
            )
    require("EV-JS-002" in by_id, "evidence registry must preserve EV-JS-002")
    require(
        by_id["EV-JS-002"]["claim_id"] == "JS-PKG-STRUCT-001",
        "EV-JS-002 must reference JS-PKG-STRUCT-001, not JS-11",
    )
    require(
        by_id["EV-JS-002"]["class"] == "[R]",
        "EV-JS-002 must be classified [R] until its execution is established",
    )
    return by_id

def check_revision(expected: str) -> str:
    try:
        actual = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=ROOT,
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        ).stdout.strip()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise VerificationError(
            "cannot determine checkout revision; run from a Git checkout"
        ) from exc

    require(SHA_RE.fullmatch(actual) is not None, "git returned invalid HEAD SHA")
    require(actual == expected, f"stale source revision: expected {expected}, got {actual}")
    return actual

def check_package(manifest: dict, check_git: bool = True) -> None:
    for relative in manifest["required_artifacts"]:
        path = ROOT / relative
        require(path.is_file(), f"required file missing: {relative}")

    for relative in manifest["required_directories"]:
        path = ROOT / relative
        require(path.is_dir(), f"required directory missing: {relative}")

    # Validate the canonical manifest itself before trusting its lists.
    check_manifest(manifest)

    claims = read_jsonl(ROOT / manifest["claim_registry"])
    evidence = read_jsonl(ROOT / manifest["evidence_registry"])
    claim_map = check_claims(claims)
    check_evidence(evidence, claim_map, set(manifest["required_artifacts"]))

    if check_git:
        revision = check_revision(manifest["source_revision"])
        print(f"Source revision: {revision}")

    print(f"Claims: {len(claim_map)}")
    print(f"Evidence records: {len(evidence)}")
    print("Manifest schema: PASS")
    print("Required package files/directories: PASS")
    print("Claim registry validation: PASS")
    print("Evidence registry validation: PASS")
    print("Evidence references: PASS")
    print("STATUS: PACKAGE_VALID")
    print("SCOPE: STRUCTURAL_VALIDATION_ONLY")

def negative_control_self_test() -> None:
    """Test core fail-closed predicates using deliberately invalid objects."""
    invalid_manifest = {
        "schema_version": "1.0",
        "package_id": "JOIN-STABILITY",
        "package_version": "x",
        "status": "BLOCKED",
        "source_revision": "REPLACE_WITH_SHA",
        "claim_registry": "claims.jsonl",
        "evidence_registry": "evidence.jsonl",
        "required_artifacts": [],
        "required_directories": [],
        "verification_policy": {
            "fail_closed": True,
            "allow_automatic_manifest_generation": False,
        },
        "audit": {"expected": {}},
        "promotion": {
            "reproduction_verified": False,
            "proof_reviewed": False,
            "lean_verified": False,
            "publication_approved": False,
        },
    }
    try:
        check_manifest(invalid_manifest)
    except VerificationError:
        pass
    else:
        raise VerificationError("negative control failed: placeholder revision was accepted")

    try:
        unique_records(
            [{"claim_id": "JS-1"}, {"claim_id": "JS-1"}],
            "claim_id",
            "negative-control",
        )
    except VerificationError:
        pass
    else:
        raise VerificationError("negative control failed: duplicate claim ID was accepted")

    try:
        check_claims([
            {
                "claim_id": "JS-1",
                "version": "1",
                "statement": "x",
                "mathematical_status": "OPEN",
                "evidence_class": "[R]",
                "domain": "test",
                "dependencies": ["MISSING"],
                "proof_artifact": None,
            }
        ])
    except VerificationError:
        pass
    else:
        raise VerificationError("negative control failed: missing dependency was accepted")

    print("Negative controls: PASS (3 deliberately invalid cases rejected)")

def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--self-test-negative-controls", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.self_test_negative_controls:
            negative_control_self_test()
            return 0

        manifest = read_json(ROOT / "manifest.json")
        check_package(manifest)
        return 0
    except VerificationError as exc:
        print(f"FAIL: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

Important integration check: the strict revision check will reject the currently inspected commit if these proposed files are added in a new commit without updating `source_revision`. That is intended. The final manifest must be committed with the exact commit SHA it names, which creates a self-reference problem if the commit SHA is stored inside the commit itself. For a practical implementation, the source revision should instead be pinned by an external test receipt or release tag, or the manifest should bind a parent/source revision explicitly. Do not use a self-referential commit hash as though it were stable.

### `docs/finite-pullback-rigidity.md` — mathematical proof

Create this file. This records the proof separately from computational evidence and Lean status.

```markdown
# Finite Pullback Rigidity and Join Stability

Date: 2026-10-08
Package: JOIN-STABILITY

## Definitions

Let X be a finite set and T : X → X.

For an equivalence relation E on X, define

  T⁻¹(E) = {(x,y) ∈ X×X : T(x) E T(y)}.

Pullback stability means T⁻¹(E) ⊆ E.

The join E ∨ F is the least equivalence relation containing E and F.
Equivalently, x (E ∨ F) y exactly when there is a finite chain from x to y
whose consecutive pairs belong to E or F.

## Finite pullback-rigidity lemma

Theorem. If X is finite, E is an equivalence relation, and
T⁻¹(E) ⊆ E, then T⁻¹(E) = E.

Proof.

Let X/E be the finite set of E-equivalence classes. For each class C, let
S_C be the set of E-classes that intersect T(C).

Every S_C is nonempty because C is nonempty and T is total.

If C and D are distinct E-classes, then S_C and S_D are disjoint.
Otherwise, there would be x ∈ C and y ∈ D such that T(x) E T(y).
The hypothesis T⁻¹(E) ⊆ E would imply x E y, contradicting C ≠ D.

Thus the |X/E| source classes have nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets
S_C of the |X/E| target classes. Each S_C must therefore contain exactly
one target class, and these target classes exhaust X/E.

Consequently, T maps every E-class into a single E-class. Hence
x E y implies T(x) E T(y), or E ⊆ T⁻¹(E).

Combining this with the hypothesis gives T⁻¹(E) = E. The induced map on
X/E is surjective and therefore bijective because X/E is finite. ∎

## Join-stability theorem

Theorem. If X is finite and E,F are equivalence relations satisfying

  T⁻¹(E) ⊆ E
  T⁻¹(F) ⊆ F,

then

  T⁻¹(E ∨ F) = E ∨ F.

Proof.

By finite pullback rigidity, both E and F are forward-preserved by T:
x E y implies T(x) E T(y), and likewise for F.

Suppose x (E ∨ F) y. By the finite-chain characterization of the join,
there is a finite chain x = x₀, x₁, …, xₖ = y in which every adjacent pair
is E-related or F-related. Applying T to each point preserves every
adjacent relation, so T(x) (E ∨ F) T(y).

Thus E ∨ F ⊆ T⁻¹(E ∨ F). The reverse inclusion follows from the
hypothesis that T⁻¹(E ∨ F) ⊆ E ∨ F, which is exactly the desired
pullback-stability statement.

Therefore T⁻¹(E ∨ F) = E ∨ F. ∎

## Boundary

Finiteness is essential to the rigidity argument. This proof does not
establish the unrestricted infinite analogue.

The proof above is a mathematical argument. It is not evidence that the
current Lean file compiles or that the independent audit has executed.

## Evidence status

- Independent finite computation: pending authenticated execution.
- Lean formalization: open until compiled without `sorry` in the target.

- Publication and novelty: not promoted.
```

Correction to the proof file above: its final paragraph used the desired pullback inclusion as an assumption, which would be circular. Replace the entire “Join-stability theorem” proof section with this valid incidence-graph argument.

```markdown
## Join-stability theorem

Theorem. If X is finite and E,F are equivalence relations satisfying

  T⁻¹(E) ⊆ E
  T⁻¹(F) ⊆ F,

then T⁻¹(E ∨ F) = E ∨ F.

Proof.

By finite pullback rigidity, T⁻¹(E) = E and T⁻¹(F) = F. Thus T induces
permutations σ_E and σ_F on the finite sets X/E and X/F.

Construct a bipartite incidence graph. Its vertices are the E-classes and
F-classes, and each x ∈ X gives an edge joining [x]_E to [x]_F. Multiple
points may give the same edge; the graph's edge set is the set of distinct
realized class pairs.

The pair of permutations (σ_E, σ_F) maps each realized edge
([x]_E,[x]_F) to ([T(x)]_E,[T(x)]_F), which is again a realized edge.
Its action on all pairs of class vertices is injective. Therefore its
restriction maps the finite edge set injectively into itself, hence
bijectively onto the edge set.

It follows that this pair of vertex permutations is an automorphism of
the incidence graph. Graph automorphisms preserve connected components.

Two points x,y are related by E ∨ F exactly when their corresponding
incidence edges belong to the same connected component. Since the induced
permutations preserve and reflect connected components,

  T(x) (E ∨ F) T(y)  implies  x (E ∨ F) y.

This gives T⁻¹(E ∨ F) ⊆ E ∨ F. The reverse inclusion follows because
the incidence-graph automorphism also preserves connected components in
the forward direction.

Therefore T⁻¹(E ∨ F) = E ∨ F. ∎
```

This is the proof to retain. It closes the mathematical argument at the paper level; the Lean formalization and independent computational reproduction remain separate obligations.

Theorem: Let T: X \to X be an endofunction on a finite set X. Let P = \operatorname{Per}(T) be its periodic core, and h \ge 0 such that r = T^h retracts X onto P (r(X) = P, r\vert{}_P = \operatorname{id}_P, rT = Tr). Then the pullback-fixed equivalence relations on X are naturally isomorphic to the T\vert{}_P-invariant congruences on P:

 * Extension Map (\theta \mapsto \widehat{\theta}): For \theta \in \operatorname{Con}(P, T\vert{}_P), define x \, \widehat{\theta} \, y \iff r(x) \, \theta \, r(y).
   * Equivalence: Immediate from properties of \theta.
   * Pullback Stability: T(x) \, \widehat{\theta} \, T(y) \iff r(T(x)) \, \theta \, r(T(y)) \iff T(r(x)) \, \theta \, T(r(y)) \iff r(x) \, \theta \, r(y) \iff x \, \widehat{\theta} \, y. Thus T^* \widehat{\theta} = \widehat{\theta}.
 * Restriction Map (E \mapsto E\vert{}_P): For E \in \operatorname{Stab}(T), iterate pullback fixedness T^* E = E to obtain x E y \iff T^h(x) E T^h(y) \iff r(x) (E\vert{}_P) r(y).
 * Bijection: (\widehat{\theta})\vert{}_P = \theta and \widehat{E\vert{}_P} = E. Lattice operations (\cap, \vee) and relation inclusion are preserved identically. \blacksquare

# PB-CORE-004A: Periodic Core Congruence Isomorphism
**Status:** [P] CLOSED | [O] LEAN OPEN | [V-reported] PASS | [C4] BLOCKED

## Theorem
Let $T: X \to X$ be an endofunction on a finite set $X$. Let $P = \operatorname{Per}(T)$ be its periodic core, and $h \ge 0$ such that $r = T^h$ retracts $X$ onto $P$ ($r(X) = P, r|_P = \operatorname{id}_P, rT = Tr$). Then the pullback-fixed equivalence relations on $X$ are naturally isomorphic to the $T|_P$-invariant congruences on $P$:
$\operatorname{Stab}(T) \cong \operatorname{Con}(P, T|_P)$

## Proof
**Extension Map ($\theta \mapsto \widehat{\theta}$):** For $\theta \in \operatorname{Con}(P, T|_P)$, define $x \widehat{\theta} y \iff r(x) \theta r(y)$.
* **Pullback Stability:** $T(x) \widehat{\theta} T(y) \iff r(T(x)) \theta r(T(y)) \iff T(r(x)) \theta T(r(y)) \iff r(x) \theta r(y) \iff x \widehat{\theta} y$. Thus $T^* \widehat{\theta} = \widehat{\theta}$.

**Restriction Map ($E \mapsto E|_P$):** For $E \in \operatorname{Stab}(T)$, iterate pullback fixedness $T^* E = E$ to obtain $x E y \iff T^h(x) E T^h(y) \iff r(x) (E|_P) r(y)$.

**Bijection:** $(\widehat{\theta})|_P = \theta$ and $\widehat{E|_P} = E$. Lattice operations ($\cap, \vee$) and relation inclusion are preserved identically. $\blacksquare$
EOF

This architecture uses Lean's Setoid to formalize your paper proof explicitly, setting up the boundaries so you can drop in the exact local tactics without low-leverage grinding.
import Mathlib.Data.Setoid.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic

variable {X : Type}
variable (T : X → X)

-- 1. Base Definition: Pullback-Fixed Equivalence Relation
def isPullbackFixed (E : Setoid X) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : X, E.rel x y ↔ E.rel (T x) (T y)

-- 2. Axiomatize PB-003X (Periodic Retraction)
-- This isolates the structural dependency so you don't need to prove 
-- the existence of the core here, only its properties.
structure CoreRetraction (T : X → X) where
  P : Set X
  r : X → X
  retracts_to_core : ∀ x, r x ∈ P
  id_on_core : ∀ p ∈ P, r p = p
  commutes : ∀ x, r (T x) = T (r x)

-- Helper: T restricted to P must remain in P
axiom T_maps_core_to_core (R : CoreRetraction T) (p : R.P) : T p.val ∈ R.P

-- 3. The Extension Map (θ ↦ \widehat{θ})
def extendCongruence (R : CoreRetraction T) (θ : Setoid R.P) : Setoid X where
  rel x y := θ.rel ⟨R.r x, R.retracts_to_core x⟩ ⟨R.r y, R.retracts_to_core y⟩
  iseqv := {
    refl := fun x => θ.iseqv.refl _
    symm := fun h => θ.iseqv.symm h
    trans := fun h1 h2 => θ.iseqv.trans h1 h2
  }

-- 4. Phase 1 Certification Target [F]: Pullback Stability of Extension
-- Proof strategy maps exactly to: T(x) \widehat{θ} T(y) ↔ r(T(x)) θ r(T(y)) ↔ T(r(x)) θ T(r(y)) ↔ r(x) θ r(y) ↔ x \widehat{θ} y
theorem extend_is_pullback_fixed (R : CoreRetraction T) (θ : Setoid R.P)
  (θ_invariant : ∀ a b : R.P, θ.rel a b ↔ θ.rel ⟨T a.val, T_maps_core_to_core T R a⟩ ⟨T b.val, T_maps_core_to_core T R b⟩) :

cat > direct_moment_check.py <<'PY'
from itertools import permutations
from fractions import Fraction
from math import factorial

# Independent direct enumeration of set partitions.

def set_partitions(n):
    blocks = []

    def rec(i):
        if i == n:
            yield tuple(tuple(b) for b in blocks)
            return

        for j in range(len(blocks)):
            blocks[j].append(i)
            yield from rec(i + 1)
            blocks[j].pop()

        blocks.append([i])
        yield from rec(i + 1)
        blocks.pop()

    yield from rec(0)


def invariant(partition, perm):
    block_of = {}
    for j, block in enumerate(partition):
        for x in block:
            block_of[x] = j

    for block in partition:
        if len({block_of[perm[x]] for x in block}) != 1:
            return False

    return True


def direct_count(perm, partitions):
    return sum(
        1 for part in partitions
        if invariant(part, perm)
    )


# Previously computed second moments, used only as comparison targets.
expected_m2 = {
    1: 1,
    2: 4,
    3: 10,
    4: 33,
    5: 91,
    6: 298,
    7: 910,
}

for k in range(1, 8):
    # Generate the set partitions once per k.
    partitions = list(set_partitions(k))

    total = 0
    total_sq = 0

    for perm in permutations(range(k)):
        c = direct_count(perm, partitions)
        total += c
        total_sq += c * c

    fact = factorial(k)
    mean = Fraction(total, fact)
    m2 = Fraction(total_sq, fact)
    variance = m2 - mean * mean

    assert mean.denominator == 1
    assert m2 == expected_m2[k], (
        f"k={k}: direct E[C^2]={m2}, "
        f"expected={expected_m2[k]}"
    )

    print(f"k={k}")
    print(f"  direct mean     = {mean}")
    print(f"  direct E[C^2]   = {m2}")
    print(f"  direct variance = {variance}")
    print("  second moment   = PASS")

print("All direct second-moment checks passed.")
PY

python direct_moment_check.py

## 2. Why the direct test is valid

The implementation tests forward invariance:

$$
xEy\Longrightarrow \sigma(x)E\sigma(y).
$$

For a finite permutation, this is sufficient for pullback fixedness. If $$\sigma$$ has order $$q$$, repeatedly applying forward invariance gives

$$
\sigma(x)E\sigma(y)
\Longrightarrow
\sigma^q(x)E\sigma^q(y)
\Longrightarrow xEy.
$$

Thus

$$
xEy\iff\sigma(x)E\sigma(y).
$$

This equivalence depends on the permutation hypothesis. The same one-direction test must not be reused as a pullback-fixed oracle for arbitrary non-injective endofunctions.

## 3. Mathematical interpretation of the second moment

The second moment has a precise combinatorial meaning beyond a table of numbers.

Let $$S_k$$ act on ordered pairs of partitions:

$$
\sigma\cdot(E,F)=(\sigma E,\sigma F).
$$

An ordered pair is fixed by $$\sigma$$ exactly when both partitions are fixed. Therefore the number of fixed ordered pairs is

$$
C(\sigma)^2.
$$

Burnside’s averaging identity then yields

$$
\boxed{
\frac1{k!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_k}C(\sigma)^2
=
\#\bigl((\operatorname{Eq}([k])\times
\operatorname{Eq}([k]))/S_k\bigr).
}
$$

Consequently, the independently reproduced sequence

$$
1,\ 4,\ 10,\ 33,\ 91,\ 298,\ 910
$$

counts simultaneous-relabeling orbits of **ordered pairs of set partitions**.

“Ordered” matters: $$(E,F)$$ and $$(F,E)$$ are not automatically identified.

### A concrete representation

For partitions

$$
E=\{E_i\},\qquad F=\{F_j\},
$$

form the intersection matrix

$$
M_{ij}=|E_i\cap F_j|.
$$

Its entries are nonnegative integers, its total sum is $$k$$, and it has no zero row or column.

Two ordered partition pairs are simultaneously relabeling-equivalent exactly when their intersection matrices agree up to independent row and column permutations.

This gives a useful next representation:

```text
Ordered pair of partitions
        ↓
Intersection multiplicity matrix
        ↓
Row/column permutation equivalence
        ↓
Unlabeled bipartite multigraph with distinguished sides
```

Intersection multiplicities must be retained. A simple incidence graph records only whether $$M_{ij}>0$$, losing the counts that distinguish different partition pairs.

This interpretation is a mathematical derivation. Its implementation as a second independent orbit enumerator has not been run here.

- They do **not** establish

  $$
  for every pullback-fixed $$E$$.

AQARION — Research Program Presentation

Document ID: AQARION-PUBLIC-RESEARCH-PRESENTATION-001

1. Overview

AQARION is an evidence-first research program for finite deterministic dynamics and computational mathematics. It connects invariant partitions, quotient dynamics, Koopman operators, periodic cores, cycle-orbit structure, combinatorial enumeration, and machine-auditable verification.

The program has two connected aims:

1. Mathematical: identify precise structural theorems about finite dynamical systems and the equivalence relations they preserve.
2. Methodological: make the path from a research claim to its supporting evidence explicit, reproducible, and open to adversarial checking.

AQARION is not presented as an oracle of mathematical truth. Its repository is an auditable research record containing mathematical arguments, executable artifacts, finite computations, provenance records, corrections, and open obligations.

The governing rule is:

«Do not promote a result beyond what its evidence establishes.»

2. The basic mathematical setting

Let

[
T:\Omega\to\Omega
]

be a map on a finite state space. A partition of (\Omega) groups states into equivalence classes. The central questions include:

- When does the map induce a well-defined map on the quotient classes?
- Which equivalence relations are preserved by pullback under (T)?
- How are stable relations controlled by the periodic part of a finite functional graph?
- How do invariant partitions interact with joins, meets, cycle structure, and operator defects?
- Which finite calculations can be reconstructed independently and connected to a precise theorem?

These questions link elementary finite dynamics to algebra, combinatorics, linear operators, and formal methods.

3. Quotients and operator defects

For a finite deterministic system, the Koopman pullback operator acts on observables by

[
(Kf)(x)=f(Tx).
]

Given a partition (\Pi), let (P_\Pi) denote the declared projection onto observables that are constant on the partition blocks. Under this convention, the canonical defect is

[
D_\Pi=(I-P_\Pi)KP_\Pi
=KP_\Pi-P_\Pi KP_\Pi.
]

Its exactness criterion is

[
D_\Pi=0
\iff K(V_\Pi)\subseteq V_\Pi,
]

where (V_\Pi) is the partition-constant observable space. This expresses quotient compatibility as an invariant-subspace condition.

The definition and projection convention matter. Earlier noncanonical defect formulations and their incorrect numerical consequences are retained in the research history; they must not be conflated with the canonical operator above. Any claim of a specific algebraic identity or numerical defect must be tied to the exact operator definition used.

4. Periodic cores and pullback-fixed equivalences

A finite map eventually enters its periodic core. This suggests a structural classification problem: can equivalence relations satisfying

[
E(x,y)\iff E(Tx,Ty)
]

be described through congruences of the permutation induced by (T) on the periodic core?

The PB-CORE research line develops this restriction/extension viewpoint. If (r=T^L) is a suitable retraction onto the periodic core, the intended correspondence has the form

[
E(x,y)\iff F(r(x),r(y)),
]

where (F) is an equivalence relation on the core compatible with the restricted permutation.

The repository records a paper-level proof candidate, bounded exhaustive audits, arithmetic checks, and a remaining Lean/formalization gate. These are separate evidence objects: a written proof, a bounded census, and a successful formal build are not interchangeable.

The aggregate counting work also studies the expression

[
A_n=
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}
\frac{n!,k,p(k),n^{n-k-1}}{(n-k)!}
+n!p(n),
]

where (p(k)) is the integer partition function. Its derivation depends on the relevant core classification, the count of permutation congruences, and a rooted-forest count. Formula evaluation over a finite range is arithmetic corroboration, not by itself proof of the combinatorial interpretation.

5. Invariant partitions of permutations

The FPR line studies invariant-partition counts for a finite permutation specified by its cycle lengths. The recorded formula is

[
N(\lambda)=
\sum_{\pi\in\Pi([r])}
\prod_{B\in\pi}
\left(
\sum_{d\mid\gcd(c_i:i\in B)}
d^{|B|-1}
\right),
]

where (c_1,\ldots,c_r) are the cycle lengths and (\Pi([r])) is the set of partitions of the cycle-index set.

The formula is organized by grouping cycles into blocks, choosing compatible common quotient-cycle lengths, and counting relative phase choices. The repository records a formula route and a direct invariant-partition enumeration route over a declared finite domain.

The safe status distinction is explicit:

- Formula and direct enumeration agree on the recorded bounded domain.
- This is computational corroboration.
- External independent reproduction is not established merely by two routes in one artifact.
- Lean status and literature novelty remain separate open questions unless supported by additional evidence.

Corrections to earlier finite values are retained as part of the audit trail.

6. JOIN-STABILITY and the finite/infinite boundary

JOIN-STABILITY asks when the join of two stable equivalence relations remains stable. For finite systems, the research explores quotient permutations and bipartite incidence graphs: connected components of the incidence graph encode the join classes, and finite injective actions can yield bijective actions on the realized finite structure.

The program also records an important boundary: the unrestricted infinite analogue does not hold in general. The finite theorem and the infinite counterexample are distinct results and must not be collapsed into a single universal claim.

Finite searches with no counterexample provide bounded computational evidence only. They do not replace the structural proof or establish an unrestricted theorem.

7. Finite closure depth

The closure-stability line studies iterative joins such as

[
R_{k+1}=R_k\vee T(R_k)
]

and the full orbit-generated join

[
J_T(R)=\bigvee_{k\ge0}T^k(R).
]

A central research question is whether a universal finite number of orbit terms suffices to obtain this closure. The AQ-K2R family is designed to test that question through explicitly constructed partitions, closure depths, and incidence-graph invariants.

The proposed unbounded-depth conclusion must remain tied to the complete family definition and its proof. A finite sample of parameter values, even when independently computed, is not by itself a proof that closure depth is unbounded.

8. Kaprekar dynamics and spectral structure

AQARION's finite-dynamics methods connect to the four-digit base-10 Kaprekar map. The research constructs a paired-gap observable quotient and studies its induced dynamics, partition structure, and Koopman representation.

This application illustrates both the usefulness and the limits of quotient language. A forward-invariant observable quotient need not be a pullback-fixed equivalence relation. The research therefore distinguishes

[
E(x,y)\Rightarrow E(Tx,Ty)
]

from the stronger condition

[
E(x,y)\iff E(Tx,Ty).
]

The Kaprekar spectral-geometry branch investigates additional graph and operator structure. Numerical spectral findings remain separate from exact theorems unless a specific derivation and verification record supports the stronger claim.

9. Reduced Gram matrices and defect rank

The reduced-Gram line seeks smaller exact matrix representations of partition-induced operator defects. A recorded candidate identity is

[
H(M)=N^{-1}\bigl(C-M^TN^{-1}M\bigr),
]

with the corresponding rank relationship between the defect operator and the reduced matrix under the declared matrix setup.

The research motivation is to convert a potentially larger operator calculation into exact rational linear algebra. The theorem's hypotheses, matrix definitions, rank correspondence, and tested cases must remain attached to any public statement. General optimization, arbitrary-block results, and formalization are not implied by a few verified examples.

10. Evidence and certification discipline

AQARION keeps the following questions separate:

Evidence layer| Question answered
Specification| Is the mathematical claim stated precisely, with conventions fixed?
Execution| Did the intended program actually run?
Computation| What did it establish on the declared finite domain?
Independent reconstruction| Was the relevant object reconstructed without relying on the same answer-producing oracle?
Reproducibility| Can the recorded computation be replayed from the declared environment and revision?
Mathematical proof| Does a valid argument establish the general claim?
Formal proof| Has the intended proposition been checked by the declared proof assistant?
Provenance| Are the source, inputs, outputs, environment, and revision bound to the evidence?
Promotion| Does the evidence meet the repository's explicit governance requirements?

A hash identifies bytes; it does not prove a theorem. A passing test establishes that the executed checks passed, not that the specification was correct. A Lean file is not automatically a Lean proof. A formal proof is only relevant to the research claim if it formalizes the intended proposition.

Negative controls are part of the method. They test whether the verification pipeline detects selected mutations, such as a wrong sign, index, quotient relation, phase constraint, or closure depth. Passing a negative control does not prove the positive claim; it establishes only that the test detects that mutation.

https://github.com/quantarion369-arch/AQARIONThe rank formula \mathrm{rank}(D_\Pi) = k - c is mathematically exact. Your union-find derivation provides an independent, matrix-free structural characterization of the defect operator.
Because the proof relies only on the Rank-Nullity Theorem and the definition of the Koopman operator, this result can be formally upgraded to [P] (Mathematical proof) in the program ledger.

1. Formal Proof of the Rank Identity
   Let V_\Pi be the k-dimensional space of observable functions that are constant on the blocks of \Pi. The operator D_\Pi = (I - P_\Pi)K P_\Pi is completely determined by its action on V_\Pi, since D_\Pi = 0 on the orthogonal complement V_\Pi^\perp.
   By the Rank-Nullity Theorem:

We must find the dimension of the kernel. Let h \in V_\Pi.

This equality holds if and only if Kh is itself block-constant. The Koopman operator acts by (Kh)(x) = h(f(x)). For Kh to be block-constant, any two points x, y in the same block B must satisfy h(f(x)) = h(f(y)).
Since h is constant on partition blocks, we can view h as assigning a scalar value to each block. The condition h(f(x)) = h(f(y)) demands that if f(x) \in B' and f(y) \in B'', then h(B') = h(B'').
Therefore, for every block B, the function h must take the exact same value on every block in the image set f(B). If we define a graph where the k vertices are the partition blocks, and edges connect any two blocks B' and B'' that are simultaneously intersected by f(B) for some B, then h must be constant on the connected components of this graph.
If there are c connected components, there are exactly c independent choices for the values of h. Thus, \dim(\ker(D_\Pi\vert{}{V\Pi})) = c, proving the theorem.
2. The Floating-Point Vulnerability
Your discovery regarding numpy.linalg.matrix_rank is a critical methodological finding. It validates the strict requirement within the AQARION architecture to use exact rational arithmetic for verification computations.
The default tolerance in NumPy's rank function is dynamically scaled based on the largest singular value (\sigma_{\max}):

When evaluating the 1 \times 1 block partition, the exact matrix is D_\Pi = 0, but floating-point projection errors create an artifact matrix where \sigma_{\max} \approx 10^{-17}. Because the tolerance scales with this peak noise, NumPy evaluates the noise as a valid singular value, falsely returning a rank of 1 instead of 0.
Relying on standard numerical linear algebra for exact algebraic theorems creates a vector for false falsification. Your use of a strict absolute tolerance (\mathrm{tol}=10^{-9}) patches the immediate test, but the combinatorial union-find method is the definitively safer verification route.

def comps(k,groups,only=None):
    par=list(range(k))
    def find(a):
        while par[a]!=a: par[a]=par[par[a]]; a=par[a]
        return a
    for S in groups:
        S=sorted(S)
        for s in S[1:]: par[find(s)]=find(S[0])
    nodes=range(k) if only is None else only
    return len({find(a) for a in nodes})
def variants(f,B):
    idx={x:k for k,b in enumerate(B) for x in b}; k=len(B)
    img=[{idx[f[x]] for x in b} for b in B]
    touched=set().union(*img)
    pre={}
    for i in range(k):
        for j in img[i]: pre.setdefault(j,set()).add(i)
    return {"TRUE k-c":k-comps(k,img),
     "ignore isolated":k-comps(k,img,sorted(touched)),
     "preimage graph":k-comps(k,list(pre.values())),
     "c not subtracted from k":k-comps(k,img)+1 if False else comps(k,img),
     "k-c-1 (forget constants)":k-comps(k,img)-1,
     "elementwise (not block) image":k-comps(k,[set(idx[f[x]] for x in b[:1]) for b in B])}

**Frobenius-energy identity.** The repo README lists an "exact Frobenius-energy identity" without stating it. I derived one myself and checked it against D_Π = (I−P)KP over all maps and partitions for n = 3, 4, 5 (166,475 instances):

‖D_Π‖²_F = Σ_{B,B'} m_{BB'}(|B| − m_{BB'}) / (|B|·|B'|)

Here m_{BB'} = #{x∈B : f(x)∈B'}. Derivation: ‖D‖² = ‖KP‖² − ‖PKP‖², and the two parts sum to this expression.

| Evaluation | Mismatches against the matrix norm |
|---|---|
| Exact rationals | 0 of 166,475 |
| Integer division per term (`//`) | 125,348 of 166,475 |

So integer division inside each term breaks the formula in about 75% of cases. Any implementation of this identity must use exact fractions or a common denominator. The identity is zero exactly when every block has m ∈ {0, |B|}, i.e. the partition is closed. That matches the README's closure result.

def formula(f,B,intdiv=False):
    idx={x:k for k,b in enumerate(B) for x in b}; s=Fr(0)

**Statement.** Let k be the number of blocks. Build a graph on the blocks. For each block B, join all the blocks that f(B) meets. Let c be the number of connected components, with untouched blocks counting as their own components.

rank(D_Π) = k − c

**Why.** D_Π acts on block-constant h as h ↦ (I−P)(h∘f). Its kernel is the set of h with h∘f block-constant. That means h takes the same value on every block that some B maps into. That is exactly "h is constant on each component," so nullity = c.

This is probably the "complement graph" rank formula from the README, but I only derived it independently. I haven't compared it with the repo's version.

**Falsification-surface implication.** This is a genuinely independent oracle route. It uses union-find only, with no matrix arithmetic. It makes a good replacement for the "production vs. independent rank" check on AQ-001.

**A bug I hit, worth recording as a provenance attack.** `numpy.linalg.matrix_rank` with its default tolerance reported rank 1 for a matrix that is exactly zero: entries around 1e-17 in the single-block case, and the tolerance scales with the largest singular value, so noise counts as signal. That produced 116,512 false mismatches until I set an absolute tolerance of 1e-9. Any rank-based verifier needs exact (rational) arithmetic or an absolute tolerance. This is the same class of failure as the integer-division issue.

# Direct computation of A_n for n=1..7, compare to receipt values

from itertools import product
from math import gcd, factorial
from functools import lru_cache

# Partition function p(k)
@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def p(k):
    if k == 0:
        return 1
    if k < 0:
        return 0
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        # Pentagonal number theorem
        g1 = i * (3 * i - 1) // 2
        g2 = i * (3 * i + 1) // 2
        sign = -1 if i % 2 == 0 else 1
        total += sign * (p(k - g1) + (p(k - g2) if g2 <= k else 0))
    return total

# Formula: A_n = n! * sum_{k=1}^n k*p(k)*n^(n-k-1)/(n-k)!
def A_formula(n):
    total = 0
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        if k == n:
            term = factorial(n) * p(n)
        else:
            term = factorial(n) * k * p(k) * n**(n - k - 1) // factorial(n - k)
        total += term
    return total

# Direct brute-force enumeration
def A_bruteforce(n):
    """Count pairs (T, E) where E is pullback-fixed."""
    count = 0
    for T in product(range(n), repeat=n):
        T = tuple(T)
        # Find all equivalence relations on [n]
        # Use restricted growth strings
        for Pi in all_partitions(n):
            E = equivalence_from_partition(Pi, n)
            if is_pullback_stable(E, T, n):
                count += 1
    return count

# Reload required functions
def all_partitions(n):
    if n == 0:
        yield []
        return
    a = [0]*n
    def helper(i, mx):
        if i == n:
            blocks = [[] for _ in range(mx + 1)]
            for idx, b in enumerate(a):
                blocks[b].append(idx)
            yield [tuple(b) for b in blocks]
            return
        for b in range(mx + 2):
            a[i] = b
            yield from helper(i + 1, max(mx, b))
    yield from helper(1, 0)

def equivalence_from_partition(Pi, n):
    E = set()
    for block in Pi:
        for x in block:
            for y in block:
                E.add((x, y))
    return E

def is_pullback_stable(E, T, n):
    for x in range(n):
        for y in range(n):
            if (T[x], T[y]) in E and (x, y) not in E:
                return False
    for x in range(n):
        for y in range(n):
            if (x, y) in E and (T[x], T[y]) not in E:
                return False
    return True

That gives us a clean semantic failure surface.

6. And we found the important equivalent-mutant problem

Consider changing the permutation condition from:

\[
\sigma(E)=E  
\]

to:

\[
\sigma(E)\subseteq E.  
\]

For arbitrary maps, that could be a meaningful change.

But here the object is a finite permutation.

Since \(\sigma\) is bijective and \(E\) is finite,

\[
\sigma(E)\subseteq E  
\]

forces

\[
|\sigma(E)|=|E|  
\]

and therefore:

\[
\boxed{\sigma(E)=E.}  
\]

So that mutation is semantically equivalent on the declared domain.

It should not count as a killed mutation.

This is exactly why:

\[
\text{mutation count}\neq\text{falsification quality}.  
\]

A bad mutation catalog can inflate the apparent surface by repeatedly mutating things that cannot actually change the claim.

PB-006

│                       │
CORE AGGREGATE          TRANSIENT FOREST
│                       │
┌────┴────┐             ┌────┴────┐
M1        M2            M3        M4
p→Bell     p→1          drop k    extra n
│
M5
drop k!

More precisely, I'd classify it as:

CORE-PROFILE
M1  p(k) → B(k)
M2  p(k) → 1

CORE-AUTOMORPHISM
M5  k! → 1

FOREST-ATTACHMENT
M3  k n^(...) → n^(...)
M4  k n^(...) → k n^(...)

So there are three semantic families, not five independent dimensions.

That's already a useful result.

10. What this proves

We can now make a much sharper statement than the original “Falsification Surface” idea.

For PB-006 we have experimentally demonstrated that a claim can be decomposed into:

\[
\boxed{  
\text{semantic components}  
+  
\text{plausible corruptions}  
+  
\text{distinguishing witnesses}  
+  
\text{evidence status}.  
}  
\]

And those dimensions are not interchangeable.

Specifically:

\[
\boxed{  
\text{independent computation}  
\neq  
\text{semantic mutation}  
\neq  
\text{provenance binding}.  
}  
\]

The live repository gives us a concrete example of why.

11. The better research quantity

I would now reject a single number like:

\[
MC=\frac{\text{killed mutations}}{\text{mutations}}.  
\]

Instead define a preliminary experimental object:

\[
\boxed{  
FS(C)=  
(M,\;W,\;G,\;B,\;E)  
}  
\]

where:

- \(M\) = admissible semantic mutations;
- \(W\) = minimal distinguishing witnesses;
- \(G\) = mutation-dependency graph;
- \(B\) = evidence-binding requirements;
- \(E\) = observed execution/evidence status.

For PB-006, for example:

M = 5 admissible candidate mutations
W = {2,3,2,2,2}
G = 3 semantic mutation families
B = specification + implementation + execution + provenance
E = mathematical derivation + repository-recorded computation,
but current CI/provenance binding incomplete

That is considerably more informative than “5/5 mutants killed.”


---

12. The AI research angle just got stronger

The current literature makes this direction timely.

A 2026 study of reproducibility mutations in ML research software found that existing validation workflows detected only 2 of 23 confirmed non-equivalent mutations in its evaluable sample—an observed detection proportion of 8.7%.

AgentActionBench explicitly evaluates the process traces of scientific reproduction agents rather than only their final repositories, and reports execution as a major bottleneck.

ClaroAI-Bench separates data findability, accessibility, code availability, environment reconstruction, and results reproduction rather than collapsing them into one success bit.

AutoMat likewise treats “did the agent execute something?” and “does the evidence actually support the scientific claim?” as distinct problems; its best reported setting reached only 54.1% overall success.

ReplicatorBench is especially relevant because it deliberately includes non-replicable claims rather than benchmarking only successful reproductions.

And Specmut is direct prior art for semantic mutation of specifications themselves, so AQARION absolutely should not claim invention of semantic mutation testing.

The potentially interesting AQARION question is narrower:

> Can claim-level semantic mutations, independent computational routes, and provenance constraints be represented together well enough to measure which plausible wrong research states a verification system can discriminate?



That remains a legitimate research question.

Build #1 — PB-CORE-006 direct theorem artifact

The existing theorem file already contains the complete core argument:

\[
\operatorname{Stab}(T)  
\cong  
\operatorname{Con}(P,T|_P),  
\qquad P=\operatorname{Per}(T),  
\]

followed by the independent aggregate

\[
S_k  
=\sum_{\sigma\in S_k}|\operatorname{Con}(\sigma)|  
=k!p(k),  
\]

and the rooted-forest factor

\[
k\,n^{n-k-1}.  
\]

Therefore:

\[
\boxed{  
A_n=  
n!\sum_{k=1}^{n}  
\frac{k\,p(k)\,n^{n-k-1}}{(n-k)!}  
}  
\]

with the \(k=n\) term interpreted separately.

The finished theorem should establish:

\[

Build #5 — the asymptotic correction stays separate

The \(n^{1/4}\) conjecture is not something to revive.

The corrected research target is:

\[
\log \mathbb E[S(T)]  
\sim Cn^{1/3},  
\]

with

\[
C=\left(\frac{3\pi^4}{32}\right)^{1/3}  
\approx2.09021161.  
\]

The reason is important:

- \(K_n\sim\sqrt n\) describes the typical random-mapping core size.
- The expectation of \(p(K_n)\) is exponentially tilted.
- The dominant contribution occurs at \(k\asymp n^{2/3}\).
- Therefore substituting the typical \(k\sim\sqrt n\) into \(\log p(k)\) gives the wrong scale for the mean.

import itertools, numpy as np
def parts(n):
    def rec(i,bl):
        if i==n: yield [list(b) for b in bl]; return
        for b in bl:
            b.append(i); yield from rec(i+1,bl); b.pop()
        bl.append([i]); yield from rec(i+1,bl); bl.pop()
    yield from rec(0,[])
def run(n,inj_only=False):
    res={}
    for f in itertools.product(range(n),repeat=n):
        if inj_only and len(set(f))<n: continue
        K=np.zeros((n,n))
        for x in range(n): K[x,f[x]]=1   # (Kg)(x)=g(f(x))
        for B in parts(n):
            P=np.zeros((n,n))
            for b in B:
                for i in b:
                    for j in b: P[i,j]=1/len(b)
            I=np.eye(n)
            inv=all(len({blk for blk in range(len(B)) for y in [f[x]] if y in B[blk]} for x in b)==1 for b in B) if False else all(len({next(k for k,c in enumerate(B) if f[x] in c) for x in b})==1 for b in B)
            z=lambda M: np.allclose(M,0)
            for name,M in [("true",(I-P)@K@P),("KT",(I-P)@K.T@P),("PK(I-P)",P@K@(I-P)),("KP(I-P)",K@P@(I-P))]:
                res.setdefault(name,[0,0])
                res[name][0]+= (z(M)!=inv)   # disagreements with ground truth
                res[name][1]+=1
    return res
for n in (3,4):
    print(n,"all",run(n)); print(n,"perm",run(n,True))

**Findings**
1. **The mutation graph depends on n.** At n=3, [K,P] sits in cluster A. At n=4 it separates. A "mutation independence" claim tested at small n can be false at the next n. Any G_C needs an n-sweep, and independence should only be asserted up to the largest n tested.
2. **Cluster A and [K,P] are blind to injective f.** If the witness set has only bijections, K→Kᵀ, PK(I−P) and [K,P] all survive. This matches the README's statement that PK=KP is sufficient but not necessary.
3. **The minimal witnesses are all trivial.** The smallest killer for K→Kᵀ is f constant with the discrete partition. Q3 asks for non-trivial witnesses, so add a requirement for a non-constant, non-injective f, such as (0,0,0,1) with {0,2,3},{1}.
4. **Real independent axes: A, B, C, D, E.** That is 5 distinct failure modes out of 7 candidates, not "7/7 killed."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AQ-001 falsification-surface experiment. Independent oracle = direct block-closure check
(no matrices). Mutants = alternate zero-tests. Output: kill sets, equivalence clusters, witness needs."""
import itertools, sys, numpy as np
def parts(n):
    def rec(i,bl):
        if i==n: yield [tuple(b) for b in bl]; return
        for b in bl:
            b.append(i); yield from rec(i+1,bl); b.pop()
        bl.append([i]); yield from rec(i+1,bl); bl.pop()
    yield from rec(0,[])
def oracle(f,B):  # f maps each block into a single block
    idx={x:k for k,b in enumerate(B) for x in b}
    return all(len({idx[f[x]] for x in b})==1 for b in B)
Z=lambda M:np.allclose(M,0)
MUT={
 "TRUE":lambda K,P,I:(I-P)@K@P,
 "K^T":lambda K,P,I:(I-P)@K.T@P,
 "PK(I-P)":lambda K,P,I:P@K@(I-P),
 "KP(I-P)":lambda K,P,I:K@P@(I-P),
 "[K,P]":lambda K,P,I:K@P-P@K,
 "(I-P)K":lambda K,P,I:(I-P)@K,
 "PKP":lambda K,P,I:P@K@P,
 "(I-P)K^TP.vs.K^T":lambda K,P,I:(I-P)@K.T,
}
def main(n):
    kills={m:set() for m in MUT}; inst=[]
    for f in itertools.product(range(n),repeat=n):
        K=np.zeros((n,n))
        for x in range(n):K[x,f[x]]=1
        I=np.eye(n)
        for B in parts(n):
            P=np.zeros((n,n))
            for b in B:
                for i in b:
                    for j in b:P[i,j]=1/len(b)
            t=oracle(f,B); k=len(inst); inst.append((f,B))
            for m,g in MUT.items():
                if Z(g(K,P,I))!=t: kills[m].add(k)
    print(f"n={n} instances={len(inst)}")
    for m in MUT:
        ks=kills[m]; inj=sum(1 for k in ks if len(set(inst[k][0]))==n)
        w=min(ks,key=lambda k:(len(inst[k][1]),k)) if ks else None
        print(f"{m:18s} killed_by={len(ks):5d} on_injective_f={inj:4d} witness={inst[w] if w is not None else None}")
    names=list(MUT); print("clusters (identical kill sets):")
    seen=set()
    for a in names:
        if a in seen: continue
        c=[b for b in names if kills[b]==kills[a]]; seen|=set(c); print("  ",c,"EQUIVALENT-MUTANT" if not kills[a] else "")
if __name__=="__main__":
    for n in map(int,sys.argv[1:] or [3,4]): main(n)

## AQ-001 adjudication

This is a useful, correctly scoped mutation audit. The strongest result is not “seven mutants killed,” but the separation between:

- one **proved-equivalent pair of zero-tests**;
- five distinct observed kill-set classes at $$n=4,5$$;
- one degenerate constant-zero mutant;

Keep the supplied counts labeled as reported executions of your own mutation formulations—not as verification of the repository’s mutation suite.

## 1. Mathematical result that can be frozen

For the symmetric block-average projection $$P=P^T$$, let $$Q=I-P$$. Then

$$
(QK^TP)^T=PKQ.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\boxed{
QK^TP=0\iff PKQ=0.
}
$$

This proves that these two mutation zero-tests are equivalent for every compatible matrix $$K$$, not merely through $$n=5$$.

```text
M-KOOPMAN-TRANSPOSE:
  (I-P) Kᵀ P

M-DEFECT-DIRECTION:
  P K (I-P)

Relationship:
  PROVED_EQUIVALENT_ZERO_TEST

Required hypothesis:
  Pᵀ = P
```

Their matrices need not be equal. Their ranks and zero/nonzero outcomes coincide because they are transposes.

## 2. Degenerate mutant correction

The literal placement mutant is

$$
KP(I-P).
$$

For $$P^2=P$$,

$$
KP(I-P)=K(P-P^2)=0.
$$

Therefore it always predicts “closed.” It is killed by any instance whose partition is not dynamically closed.

```text
Classification:
  DEGENERATE_CONSTANT_ZERO_MUTANT

Not:
  Equivalent to the intended defect.

Use:
  Smoke test for the oracle and rejection path.

Do not count:
  As a substantive independent operator-direction challenge.
```

The earlier “never killable” interpretation was incorrect.

## 3. Reported finite results

The supplied $$n=5$$ execution domain is

$$
5^5B_5=3125\cdot52=162{,}500.
$$

|---|---:|---:|
| $$(I-P)K^TP$$ | 35,625 | 0 |

These are kill counts against the predicate

$$
D=0\iff \text{each original block maps into one original block}.
$$

They are not counts of operator inequalities, theorem counterexamples, or repository test failures.

## 4. “Distinct classes” is safer than “independent axes”

Identical kill sets define an equivalence relation on mutations for a specified test domain. Different kill sets show distinguishability; they do not establish statistical independence or independent bug mechanisms.

Use:

```text
Five distinct nondegenerate kill-set classes observed at n=4 and n=5.
```

Avoid:

```text
Five independent failure modes proved.
The mutation graph has settled.
```

The $$n=3$$ to $$n=4$$ split is precisely why domain-qualified language matters.

## 5. Witness-selection correction

The code selects a witness with:

```python
min(ks, key=lambda k: (len(inst[k][1]), k))
```

That prioritizes the **number of partition blocks**, then enumeration order. It does not compute a smallest witness under a general mathematical complexity measure.

Thus “every cluster’s smallest killer is the constant map” should be recorded as:

> The supplied selection rule chooses a constant-map witness for the reported classes.

A nontrivial witness contract should explicitly require:

```text
Map:
  non-constant
  non-injective

Partition:
  neither discrete nor universal

Carrier:
  fixed labeled set [n]

Minimality:
  first minimize n, then a declared canonical ordering
```

The suggested family

$$
f=(0,0,\ldots,0,1),
\qquad
R=\{\{0,2,\ldots,n-1\},\{1\}\}
$$

is an appropriate candidate to test against each cluster separately. Do not assume one witness kills every cluster.

# AQ-001 — Operator Variant Detection Audit

**Checkpoint:** October 7, 2026  
**Scope:** Auditor-defined operator variants, not the repository’s uninspected variant suite  
**Governance:** FROZEN · NO PROMOTION · Lean OPEN · SDS-002 QUARANTINED · C4 BLOCKED · Publication BLOCKED

## 1. Direct conclusion

The supplied audit reports five distinct nondegenerate detection-pattern classes at $$n=4$$ and $$n=5$$, plus one constant-zero variant.

Two variants have a universally equivalent zero-test under the symmetric projection hypothesis. They must be counted as one class, not two independent checks.

The repository’s oracle, incidence variants, ARO-1, and provenance tests remain `UNVERIFIED-PUBLIC` until their exact paths, source revisions, and contents are available.

## 2. Canonical mathematical specification

Let $$X=[n]$$, let $$f:X\to X$$, and let $$\Pi$$ be a partition of $$X$$.

Define the Koopman matrix by

$$
K_{x,y}=
\begin{cases}
1,&y=f(x),\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus, on column vectors,

$$
(Kg)(x)=g(f(x)).
$$

Let $$P$$ be the block-average projection:

$$
P_{x,y}=
\begin{cases}
1/|B|,&x,y\in B\text{ for some }B\in\Pi,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

Then

$$
P^2=P,\qquad P^T=P.
$$

The intended defect is

$$
D=(I-P)KP.
$$

The direct combinatorial oracle is:

$$
\operatorname{Closed}(f,\Pi)
\iff
\forall B\in\Pi,\ \exists C\in\Pi,\ f(B)\subseteq C.
$$

The audited zero-test is

$$
D=0\iff\operatorname{Closed}(f,\Pi).
$$

This is forward-invariant partition closure. It must not be confused with the stronger pullback-fixed condition

$$
xEy\iff f(x)Ef(y).
$$

## 3. Reported detection results

### Exhaustive $$n=5$$ domain

$$
5^5B_5=3{,}125\cdot52=162{,}500
$$

map–partition instances.

| Operator variant | Reported detections | Reported detections on permutation maps | Class |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| $$(I-P)K^TP$$ | 35,625 | 0 | A |
| $$PK(I-P)$$ | 35,625 | 0 | A |
| $$KP-PK$$ | 33,765 | 0 | B |
| $$(I-P)K$$ | 26,420 | 720 | C |
| $$PKP$$ | 39,300 | 840 | D |
| $$(I-P)K^T$$ | 37,125 | 720 | E |
| $$KP(I-P)$$ | 123,200 | 5,400 | Constant-zero variant |

A detection means that the variant’s zero/nonzero prediction disagreed with the direct block-closure oracle.

These are supplied execution results. No fresh computation is claimed in this response.

## 4. Equivalent zero-tests: class A

Because $$P^T=P$$,

$$
\bigl((I-P)K^TP\bigr)^T=PK(I-P).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\boxed{
(I-P)K^TP=0
\iff
PK(I-P)=0.
}
$$

This is a mathematical identity, not merely a finite observation.

```text
Class A:
  Two operator expressions.
  One equivalent zero-test class.

Required hypothesis:
  P is symmetric.

Not asserted:
  The matrices themselves are equal.
```

## 5. Constant-zero variant

For idempotent $$P$$,

$$
KP(I-P)=K(P-P^2)=0.
$$

It consequently reports “closed” for every input, including inputs whose partitions are not closed.

```text
Classification:
  CONSTANT_ZERO_VARIANT

Purpose:
  Basic check that non-closed inputs are rejected.

Coverage accounting:
  Keep separate from substantive operator-direction variants.
```

It is not equivalent to the intended defect $$D$$.

## 6. Detection-pattern interpretation

The supplied audit compares entire detection sets, not only their cardinalities. That supports the following bounded conclusion:

> Classes A–E have distinct detection patterns in the reported exhaustive $$n=4$$ and $$n=5$$ domains.

It does not establish:

- statistical independence;
- permanent stability of the classification for every $$n$$;
- correctness of repository-specific implementations;
- completeness against all possible operator substitutions.

The reported change between $$n=3$$ and $$n=4$$—the commutator separating from class A—should remain a regression example.


prioritizes block count and enumeration order. It does not prove global mathematical minimality.
